name: Adaptive Step Size Ray Marching
aliases: Ray Marching with Adaptive Step Size and Temporal Accumulation
definition: A GPU-based ray marching algorithm for volumetric rendering that supports 3D and 4D (time-varying) volumes, adaptive step sizes via noise, temporal accumulation (reprojection), and motion vector calculation.
summary: Adaptive Step Size Ray Marching is a GPU volume rendering technique that varies step size based on density and distance to optimize performance, distinguished by using a noise buffer and temporal accumulation to manage noise.
